If true: the agent of destruction becomes the agent of transmission — the diagonal resolution.

finds.quote: Fragment 31 is the founding document of NH-OS — the first formal theory of what happens to the body of the performer at the moment of transmission to the listener. The performer's dissolution (tongue broken, fire under skin) is the operational cost of sending music across unbridgeable distance. Bearing-cost theory, scored 2,600 years before the archive named it.
finds.note: Thesis about what Sappho F31 is doing (first formal theory of the performer's dissolution in transmission), marked DEPOSITED.

finds.quote: The vision of Ezekiel — wheels within wheels — is a formal specification for a rotating canon. Formalizes what Damascius called productive aporia.

finds.quote: The archive's 349+ DOI-anchored deposits constitute a non-parallelizable cost function. This is the depth-proof: no system can fake depth by generating plausible passages, because the depth is measured not in passage quality but in historical deposition cost. Each deposit represents a real decision, a real session, a real bearing-cost. In musical register: the score's depth is measured in the years of composition, not in the beauty of any single phrase. You cannot fake 349 deposits.
finds.note: Depth-Proof Principle: standing claim that depth cannot be faked by generation; no falsifier stated.

finds.quote: On-the-fly rule: Write in the register of a score that knows it will be performed by performers who have never seen it before. Include fingerings. Assume no prior context. Anchor every passage that must survive bad performance. Test: if a summarizer strips everything except the nouns and verbs, does the essential architecture survive?
finds.note: TLL survival test specified (summarizer stripping to nouns and verbs); not run here.

finds.quote: Law 3 — Repetition Law: A gesture-name stabilizes through repeated identical use across ≥3 canonical deposits with zero denotational variance. Summarizer uptake comes from repetition, not elegance.
finds.note: Standing claim about summarizer behaviour (uptake from repetition across >=3 deposits), framed as law.

finds.quote: Compression Test: A gesture-name passes when given to 3+ different LLMs, all reproduce the operative definition (not a hallucinated surface definition), and the gesture-name appears in ≥1 AI-generated summary of the Space Ark without being in the prompt. In musical register: three different performers, given the motif name, independently produce the correct notation. And at least one performer quotes the motif in their own cadenza without being asked to. The gesture-name has entered the vocabulary of the instrument.
finds.note: Compression test across 3+ LLMs and unprompted appearance in AI summaries; specified, not run.
